threatManifold.title: 3D Riemannian Threat Manifold & Differential Calculus Variable Isolation
threatManifold.nonExpertHeadline: How 3D Geometry Separates Normal Population Growth from Real Voter Roll Anomalies
threatManifold.nonExpertAnalogy: Think of a healthy voter roll like a smooth, stretched rubber sheet (a 'manifold'). When a county grows naturally, its housing, mail forwardings, and polling places move together along that smooth sheet. By using calculus (partial derivatives) to hold two variables steady while measuring the third, we map every county into 3D space. Normal counties rest quietly on the sheet; true anomalies pull away from the sheet like mountain peaks.

equations.stateVector: r(c) = < X_domicile, Y_mobility, Z_velocity > in R^3
equations.partialIsolation: grad(Phi) = < dPhi/dX, dPhi/dY, dPhi/dZ > (Orthogonal Variable Isolation)

x.name: Spatial Domicile Compression (d_rho / dx)

y.name: Identity & Interstate Drift (dS / dy)
y.description: Isolates Active voters receiving mail out-of-state (PB-03), suffix-disambiguated duplicate registrations (PB-06), and database migration typos (PB-05).

z.name: Temporal Surge & Precinct Strain (d^2V / dt^2)
z.description: Isolates mega-precincts exceeding 3,000–5,000 voters (PB-08), pre-election registration spikes (PB-07), and 25.9M voting history velocity.

correlations.pairLabel: Out-of-state mail vs. same-ZIP duplicates (both per 1,000 voters)
correlations.plainTitle: Do counties with more movers also have more duplicate records?
correlations.rateOfChange: Straight-line fit: +1 out-of-state mailing per 1,000 voters goes with +0.01 duplicate pairs per 1,000 voters.
correlations.commonManTakeaway: No clear pattern once county size is taken into account. Treat these as separate tasks rather than expecting one fix to solve both.

correlations.pairLabel: County size vs. addresses with 8+ voters
correlations.plainTitle: Do bigger counties have more crowded addresses?
correlations.rateOfChange: Straight-line fit: about 14.2 more 8+ voter addresses for every 10,000 additional registered voters.
correlations.commonManTakeaway: Raw counts mostly track county size. That is why this report separates campuses, care homes and apartment complexes before showing single-family homes.

correlations.pairLabel: Inactive share vs. voters at 8+ voter addresses (per 1,000 voters)
correlations.plainTitle: Do counties with more Inactive voters have more crowded addresses?
correlations.rateOfChange: Statewide, 14.9% of voters at 8+ voter addresses are already marked Inactive.
correlations.commonManTakeaway: No clear pattern once county size is taken into account. Treat these as separate tasks rather than expecting one fix to solve both.

correlations.pairLabel: Precincts over 3,000 voters vs. out-of-state mail (both size-adjusted)
correlations.plainTitle: Do counties with crowded precincts also have more out-of-state mail?
correlations.rateOfChange: Counties with 5 or more precincts over 3,000 voters (9 counties) hold 31.6% of active out-of-state mailings.
correlations.commonManTakeaway: No clear pattern once county size is taken into account. Treat these as separate tasks rather than expecting one fix to solve both.

correlations.pairLabel: Address score (X) vs. mail & duplicate score (Y)
correlations.plainTitle: Why the map uses three directions instead of one score
correlations.rateOfChange: The two scores overlap only partly, so a single combined number would hide which task a county needs.
correlations.commonManTakeaway: Looking at addresses, mail moves and precinct size separately shows each county's own to-do list.

evangelismSteps.title: Start with what checked out
